dedupe_keys.name: managing water for irrigated agriculture in the central arizona desert u s climate resilience toolkit

description: This U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit case study describes how irrigation district managers in central Arizona are adapting to a drought that has raised doubts about the Colorado River system that supports regional farming and growth. It reports that managers monitor stream gauges on Colorado River tributaries more than a thousand stream-miles away and even Colorado ski reports, track reservoir, energy and inter-sector allocation policy, and plan the mix of wells and surface water, since groundwater pumping capacity can be as limiting as supply. Managers also run only the most efficient wells, avoid pumping at the same location at once, and in 2015 some districts volunteered to forgo part of their Hoover Dam reservoir allotment or used water banking agreements. Coverage: the Phoenix area irrigation districts, with interview evidence, not data tables. Access: a free web page; the licence is not stated. Caveats: qualitative, from research at Arizona State University, with no infrastructure performance measures. It supports irrigation adaptation, operations and capacity planning studies for drought, and relates to the Orange County groundwater replenishment case study on supply alternatives in the catalogue.
